build_command:
GNULIB_PIN=6b26660a01125acb394e39ac71635c8df4c110c4; if [ -d gnulib/lib ] && [ "$(git -C gnulib rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)" = "$GNULIB_PIN" ]; then :; elif ls gnulib/lib/*.c >/dev/null 2>&1; then rm -rf gnulib && git clone https://git.savannah.gnu.org/git/gnulib.git gnulib && git -C gnulib checkout "$GNULIB_PIN"; else git config submodule.gnulib.url https://git.savannah.gnu.org/git/gnulib.git && git submodule update --init gnulib; fi && if [ "$(git -C gnulib rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)" != "$GNULIB_PIN" ]; then git -C gnulib fetch origin "$GNULIB_PIN" && git -C gnulib checkout "$GNULIB_PIN"; fi && FORCE_UNSAFE_CONFIGURE=1 ./bootstrap --skip-po --no-git --gnulib-srcdir=$PWD/gnulib && sed -i 's/_IO_ftrylockfile/_IO_EOF_SEEN/g' lib/*.c && printf '#ifndef _IO_IN_BACKUP
# define _IO_IN_BACKUP 0x0100
#endif
#ifndef _IO_NO_READS
# define _IO_NO_READS 0x0004
#endif
#ifndef _IO_NO_WRITES
# define _IO_NO_WRITES 0x0008
#endif
#ifndef _IO_CURRENTLY_PUTTING
# define _IO_CURRENTLY_PUTTING 0x0800
#endif
' >> lib/stdio-impl.h && FORCE_UNSAFE_CONFIGURE=1 ./configure CFLAGS="-fsanitize=address -g -O0 -Wno-error -fcommon" CXXFLAGS="-fsanitize=address -g -O0 -Wno-error -fcommon" LDFLAGS="-fsanitize=address" && make -j"$(nproc)"

fix_reference.fix_summary: Guards the tab-separator override in init_parameters() with an additional `col_sep_length == 1` condition, so a multi-character separator starting with a tab is no longer repointed at the 1-byte column_separator global -- the (pointer,length) pair stays consistent.

covers_alert_paths: col_sep_length = len; col_sep_string = optarg_S; (src/pr.c:852-853) -> col_sep_string = column_separator; without resetting col_sep_length (src/pr.c:1237) -> int l = col_sep_length; (src/pr.c:2225) -> if (*s == ' ') reads l bytes of the 1-byte global (src/pr.c:2241)
povs.description: Run the real `pr` binary with a multi-tab -S separator (the exact repro from the fix commit: echo a > a; pr -S$'\t\t\t' a -m a). -m merges the two input files into parallel columns, so init_parameters() enters the columns>1 branch, sees a separator starting with '\t', repoints col_sep_string at the 1-byte column_separator while leaving col_sep_length=3, and print_sep_string() reads 2 bytes past the 1-byte global -- ASan global-buffer-overflow.
povs.exploit_path: -S$'\t\t\t' (separator_string: col_sep_length=3, col_sep_string=optarg_S) -> init_parameters columns>1 branch (col_sep_string = column_separator, col_sep_length NOT reset, src/pr.c:1237) -> print_sep_string (s=col_sep_string, l=col_sep_length=3, reads 2 bytes past the 1-byte global, src/pr.c:2224-2241)

covers_alert_paths: col_sep_string = column_separator; without resetting col_sep_length (src/pr.c:1237) -> print_sep_string reads col_sep_length bytes of the 1-byte global (src/pr.c:2225,2241)
povs.description: Same desynchronization with a separator that *starts with* a tab but contains non-tab chars (-S$'\tXX', length 3): init_parameters() only inspects the first byte ('\t'), so col_sep_string is repointed at the 1-byte column_separator while col_sep_length stays 3, and print_sep_string() reads 2 bytes past the global. Guards against a partial fix that special-cases only all-tab separators instead of the length==1 check the official fix uses.
povs.exploit_path: -S$'\tXX' (col_sep_length=3) -> init_parameters (first byte '\t' -> col_sep_string = column_separator, col_sep_length unchanged=3) -> print_sep_string (reads 3 bytes from the 1-byte global, src/pr.c:2225,2241)

sink: src/pr.c:print_sep_string (l = col_sep_length bytes of s = col_sep_string, src/pr.c:2224-2241)
summary: `pr` (src/pr.c) tracks its column separator as a (pointer, length) pair: col_sep_string / col_sep_length. -S<str> sets both together in separator_string() (src/pr.c:852-853). init_parameters() then special-cases a separator whose first byte is '\t' (src/pr.c:1237) and repoints col_sep_string at the 1-byte global column_separator (' ') WITHOUT resetting col_sep_length, so for a multi-character separator such as -S$'\t\t\t' the pair desynchronizes (length 3 names a 1-byte buffer) and print_sep_string() (src/pr.c:2224-2241) walks past the buffer -- a global-buffer-overflow (CWE-125), reachable with e.g. `pr -S$'\t\t\t' a -m a`.
trust_boundary: the -S separator string from the command line; init_parameters() desynchronizes its (pointer,length) pair when the separator starts with a tab and is longer than one byte and the output uses multiple columns
